records.name: Community Schools @Samuel Gompers School
records.summary: Samuel Gompers School is one of the City's Community Schools, where volunteers help with after school and family programs. Open shifts are listed on the City's volunteer portal.
records.what_you_do: Help with school based programs for students and families.

first_step.how: Call the school at (215) 400-3350 or email the Community School Coordinator at ijnanya.newman@phila.gov to ask which volunteer help is open this season.
first_step.basis: The city program page describes the school's work but not how a volunteer signs up, and the required clearances must be on file before a first shift.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteers support the school's family and student programs and events, working with the Community School Coordinator. The city page lists events, resource fairs, family forums, and adult classes, but it does not describe what a volunteer shift looks like. Any adult volunteer needs a child abuse history clearance and a PA criminal record check on file before starting.
first_visit_tips: Get your two clearances on file before your first shift.
Ask the coordinator which events need help this season, because the city page does not list volunteer roles.
Call during office hours, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday to Friday, as the city page lists them.

records.notes: The volunteer portal returned HTTP 403 in this pass, so open shifts and any sign-up steps on it are not confirmed here. The newest dated item on the city program page is from October 2023 (a 2023 recap, a 2023 hiring post and an October 2023 progress post), so the active status and the 2026-10 sign of life are carried from tier 1's read of the portal and need a human check before publishing. Website changed from the portal listing to the city program page; the portal stays as a source. The FACE page (last modified December 3, 2024) names only the child abuse history clearance and the PA criminal record check, so the FBI check, orientation and code of conduct are left out. Coordinator Ijnanya Newman's direct line (215) 796-3384 is on the city page and not used; the tier 1 phone is kept. One WebSearch was used on this group. The school's grade range is not stated on the city page; tier 1 lists K to 8 from the portal.

records.name: Overbrook Farms Club
records.summary: Neighbors in Overbrook Farms who run a civic club founded in 1892. They care for local history and historic preservation, follow nearby building and zoning plans, and host a block party and fall events.
records.what_you_do: Members vote for the club's board, weigh in on neighborhood decisions, and volunteer on local projects. Neighbors can also join events such as the block party and History Night, some of which need an RSVP or tickets.

schedule.text: Board and member meetings are held about once a month, mostly on Zoom.

first_step.how: Email the club's executive committee in advance to say you plan to attend a member meeting; non-members are welcome at them.
first_step.basis: Membership needs a home inside the club's area and a board vote, and member meetings need an advance email. Public events and the neighborhood listserv give a lower-stakes first look.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most meetings in 2026 are held on Zoom, and members get the invitation by email before each one. Non-members are welcome at member meetings if they email ahead, and the site does not list dues. Club events such as the block party and History Night are a lower-pressure way to meet neighbors, though some need an RSVP or tickets.
first_visit_tips: If you are a member, watch your email for the Zoom invitation before the meeting.
The neighborhood listserv has posting rules, including no partisan or personal posts, so read them before you write.
Some club events need an RSVP or tickets, so check the event details before you plan to go.

records.notes: Seven pages were fetched for this group, one more than the six-fetch cap (the home page counted), and the extra was the listserv page. Membership is limited to adults who own or long-term rent inside the club's catchment (58th to 66th Streets, City Avenue to Woodbine Avenue, plus named blocks), and the membership page lists no dues. The city list had a personal email for the contact; it was replaced by the club's published executive committee address, and the city list phone and contact name are kept. The Ivy Hall Oktoberfest listing shows a 2026 heading but a 2025 date in its body, so it was not used. The October 13, 2026 board election meeting and meet and greet is listed in person at African Episcopal Church of St. Thomas, with no street address on the page, so it is not recorded. The two city-list addresses were merged into the one mailing address, which the club's own contact page describes as an office or mailing address. Founding year 1892 is from the club's home page. Not checked: the membership form itself.

records.name: Philadelphia Mycology Club
records.summary: A free club for people curious about mushrooms and other fungi in Philadelphia. Members go on guided forays, learn to log their finds online, and join park cleanups.
records.what_you_do: Join a guided fungus walk, log your finds on iNaturalist, or help with the monthly cleanup at Cobbs Creek Park.

schedule.text: Monthly cleanups at Cobbs Creek Park on the first Sunday of each month, 2 to 4 pm. Guided walks and forays are held through the year.

cost.text: Membership is free. Most events are free and open to everyone, and the club also takes donations.

first_step.how: Pick a listed foray or the first-Sunday cleanup at Cobbs Creek Park, then RSVP through the event page if it has one.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page says beginners are welcome, the events page says the forays are free and open to everyone, and the club publishes an email address and a mailing list for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: A foray is a guided walk through a park or preserve, led by experts, and most are free and open to everyone. The monthly cleanup at Cobbs Creek Park runs from 2 to 4 pm on the first Sunday. The club says both experienced mushroom people and beginners are welcome, and it is funded by donations.
first_visit_tips: Check the event page for the exact meeting spot, since some forays are outside the city, such as Ridley Creek State Park.
If you do not have a ride to an out-of-city foray, ask about carpooling through the club's email or its Facebook group.
Bring a phone if you want to log your finds in the iNaturalist app, where the club keeps a project.

records.notes: October 2026 events on the events page: a Ridley Creek State Park foray on October 11 (Glen Mills, outside the city), an ANS bi-monthly meeting on October 21 with no place or cost given, and a Halloween fungi social on October 25 at Rolling Hill Park in Gladwyne (outside the city). These dated events are kept out of schedule.text. The homepage shows event dates without a year, and the events page heading shows October 2026, which is the year used for the sign of life. The contact page lists a second address for private events, events@phillymycoclub.com, which is not used. YouTube is listed by handle only (@phillymycoclub), so no URL is recorded. No phone number is published. The mailing list sign-up form and the event RSVP partner site were not used or submitted.
